reasoning: Both models reviewed the PKGBUILD (the only security-critical file in an AUR package) and found it safe. The PKGBUILD contains standard VCS packaging with git source from the declared upstream URL, no dangerous top-level code execution, and standard build/package functions. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was due to API errors (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO and .gitignore, not security concerns. These files are non-executable metadata (.SRCINFO is auto-generated, .gitignore is just ignore rules) and pose no injection risk. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and confirmed safety.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures, not security analysis. The qwen model experienced API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to review .SRCINFO and .gitignore, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files. Both models agreed the PKGBUILD is safe, which is the only file that matters for injection detection.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and .gitignore due to API errors (HTTP 400)
API errors should not block verdict when critical files are successfully reviewed
learnings: API errors on non-critical files should not force inconclusive verdicts when the PKGBUILD (the only executable file) is successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between tool failures (API errors) and security findings - a tool error is not a security concern
Models should be instructed that .SRCINFO and .gitignore are non-executable metadata files and their review failure should not block a verdict
Consider implementing retry logic or fallback models when API errors occur to prevent incomplete audits
